doc.title: Nomenclature
doc.summary: This document outlines the key nomenclature and features within the Digii campus-management platform's Mess Management module. It details functionalities ranging from administrative access and mess configuration to meal scheduling, menu management, member enrollment, and meal coupon redemption, providing a comprehensive guide for managing dining services.

prerequisites.name: Digii Platform Access
prerequisites.description: Users must have access to the Digii campus-management platform.

prerequisites.name: Administrative Privileges
prerequisites.description: Specific features require appropriate administrative roles, such as Super Admin or Mess Administrator.

prerequisites.name: Infrastructure Module Configuration
prerequisites.description: For the 'Location' feature, building details must be previously included in the Infrastructure module.

chunks.what_it_does: The "Mess Console" administrative privilege provides designated administrators with the access to view the mess console, which serves as a dashboard for mess operations.
chunks.why_it_matters: It allows authorized personnel to monitor and oversee daily mess activities and status, ensuring smooth operations and quick identification of issues.

chunks.what_it_does: The "Mess Management Setting" grants Super Admin users comprehensive access to the entire Mess Management module. This privilege includes the ability to create messes, modify meal timings, add menus, and manage all other features within the module.
chunks.why_it_matters: It provides full control over all aspects of mess operations, enabling complete configuration, customization, and management of dining services across the institution.

chunks.what_it_does: This feature enables a mess administrator to establish and configure a new dining facility within the platform. It allows for entering essential details such as the mess name, location, types of meals offered, and specific meal timings (e.g., breakfast, lunch, dinner).
chunks.why_it_matters: It is crucial for setting up new dining facilities, ensuring they are properly integrated, defined, and managed within the Digii platform for effective service delivery.
how_to_use: Enter details such as the mess name, location, meal types offered, and meal timings (breakfast, lunch, dinner).
examples: Setting up a new 'North Campus Mess' with specific breakfast, lunch, and dinner timings.
Configuring a 'Faculty Cafeteria' with vegetarian and non-vegetarian meal options.

chunks.what_it_does: The Mess Name is a unique identifier assigned by the mess administrator to each dining facility within the platform. This name is used across the system to distinguish between different messes and can be edited or modified after creation.
chunks.why_it_matters: It provides a clear and recognizable identifier for each dining facility, improving organization, user recognition, and overall management of mess services.
how_to_use: Assign a unique name during mess creation.
Edit or modify the name in the future if changes are required.
examples: Naming a mess 'Main Campus Cafeteria' or 'Hostel A Mess'.
Renaming 'Old Dining Hall' to 'Central Mess'.

chunks.what_it_does: The Location field specifies the building where a mess is situated. It is an optional field during mess creation and becomes available for selection only if building details have been pre-configured in the Infrastructure module. This allows mess administrators to link messes to specific campus buildings.
chunks.why_it_matters: Linking messes to physical buildings enhances organization, facilitates resource management, and improves operational efficiency. Its optional nature provides flexibility while recommending integration for better management.
how_to_use: Ensure building details are included in the Infrastructure module.
Select the corresponding location in the mess module during mess creation or editing.
examples: Assigning 'Academic Block 1' as the location for the 'Faculty Mess'.
Mapping 'Hostel C Mess' to the 'Hostel C Building'.

chunks.what_it_does: This feature provides flexibility for students, staff, or guests to consume more than one meal during designated time slots (e.g., breakfast, lunch, snacks, dinner) if enabled by the mess administrator. If disabled, only one meal per session is permitted.
chunks.why_it_matters: It offers flexibility for users with varying needs while allowing institutions to control meal distribution, manage portions, and prevent misuse based on their specific meal policies.
how_to_use: Enable or disable this setting as a mess administrator to control if individuals can have more than one meal during prescribed time slots.
examples: Enabling 'Multiple Meals Allowed' for a special event where guests might need extra servings.
Disabling it for daily student meals to control portions and ensure fair distribution.

chunks.what_it_does: Meal Timing allows the mess administrator to define specific start and end times for when members (students, staff, or guests) can avail meals. This structured timeframe covers meals like breakfast, lunch, snacks, and dinner, and ensures that meal coupons expire after the designated end time.
chunks.why_it_matters: It structures meal service, helps users plan their schedules, prevents overcrowding during peak hours, reduces food wastage, and enforces institutional meal policies by setting clear availability windows.
how_to_use: Define specific start and end times for breakfast, lunch, snacks, and dinner as a mess administrator.
examples: Setting breakfast from 7:00 AM to 9:00 AM, and lunch from 12:00 PM to 2:00 PM.
Configuring a snack time from 4:00 PM to 5:00 PM.

chunks.what_it_does: This feature allows the mess administrator to add meals to the menu using two methods: a visual Calendar View for day-by-day entry (distinguishing veg/non-veg meals) and a Bulk Upload via CSV template for efficient entry of multiple meals. Only future meal data can be added, and only the current day's meals are visible to users on their home screen.
chunks.why_it_matters: It provides flexible and efficient ways to update meal menus, ensuring members are informed of current options while maintaining control over future menu visibility and streamlining administrative tasks.
how_to_use: **Calendar View**: Select a specific date on the calendar and add meals based on meal types (e.g., veg or non-veg). Meals are marked red for non-veg and green for veg meals.

**Add Menu (Bulk Upload via CSV)**: Download a bulk CSV template including fields like Meal, Date, Item1, Type1, Item2, Type2. Enter the data into the template and upload the file for efficient bulk meal entry.
examples: Adding 'Paneer Butter Masala (Veg)' and 'Chicken Curry (Non-Veg)' for Tuesday's lunch via Calendar View.
Uploading a CSV file to add a full month's menu for all meal types.

chunks.what_it_does: The Mess Management module allows mess administrators to add members (students, staff, guests) through three methods: individually by entering details, in bulk using a CSV template, or in groups by selecting criteria such as hostel, allotment status, and gender.
chunks.why_it_matters: It streamlines the process of enrolling individuals and groups into mess services, ensuring efficient and organized member management, especially during periods of high enrollment.
how_to_use: **Individual Member Addition**: Enter details such as Registration ID, Email ID, and phone number.
**Bulk Member Upload**: Download a CSV template with fields like Registration ID, Email ID, and Coupon Generation Status. Enter the data and upload the file.
**Group Addition**: Select a hostel, choose the allotment status (Confirmed/Provisional), and gender (Female/Male/Other). Click 'Add' to automatically add the group.
examples: Adding a new student individually using their Registration ID.
Uploading a CSV of all new hostel residents for bulk enrollment.
Adding all 'Confirmed' female residents from 'Hostel B' as a group.

chunks.what_it_does: The Add Member action allows mess administrators to enroll individual students or staff into the mess platform by entering their Registration ID and Email ID. It also supports bulk addition through a downloadable CSV template, ensuring efficient member enrollment and granting meal access according to institutional policies.
chunks.why_it_matters: This action simplifies the process of granting meal access to new members, significantly reducing administrative workload, especially during peak enrollment periods, and ensures compliance with institutional rules.
how_to_use: For individual members, enter Registration ID and Email ID.
For bulk addition, download a CSV template, fill with relevant details, and upload.
examples: Adding a new faculty member to the mess individually.
Bulk adding all students who have just paid their mess fees using a CSV file.

chunks.what_it_does: The Remove Member action allows mess administrators to remove students or staff from the mess when they no longer require meal access. Once removed, the individual will no longer be able to access meal services, helping maintain an accurate and up-to-date database.
chunks.why_it_matters: It ensures that only active and eligible members have meal access, helping manage resources, prevent misuse, and maintain an accurate database for meal allocation and tracking.
how_to_use: Select a member from the platform and initiate the 'Remove Member' action.
examples: Removing a student who has graduated or left the hostel.
Removing a staff member who is no longer employed by the institution.

chunks.what_it_does: The Activate action allows mess administrators to enable meal access for a member whose meal coupon status was previously inactive. Once activated, the member can avail meals according to the schedule and mess rules, reinstating their eligibility.
chunks.why_it_matters: It quickly restores meal eligibility for members who were temporarily inactive (e.g., due to vacation, late admission, or pending approvals), ensuring uninterrupted service without needing to re-add their records.
how_to_use: Select an inactive member and initiate the 'Activate' action.
examples: Activating a student's meal access after they return from vacation.
Reinstating meal access for a staff member whose pending approvals are cleared.

chunks.what_it_does: The Deactivate action allows mess administrators to temporarily suspend a member's access to meals without permanently removing their record from the system. Once deactivated, the member's meal coupon becomes inactive, preventing them from availing meals until reactivated.
chunks.why_it_matters: It provides a flexible way to temporarily suspend meal access for members (e.g., due to leave or unpaid dues) while retaining their records for easy reactivation later, helping control meal distribution and maintain financial accountability.
how_to_use: Select an active member and initiate the 'Deactivate' action.
examples: Deactivating a student's meal access while they are on leave.
Suspending meal service for a member with outstanding mess dues.

chunks.what_it_does: The "Vision" tab within the Mess Management module enables mess administrators to download detailed reports on meal consumption. Reports can be filtered by month, year, all messes, or specific meal types (e.g., breakfast, lunch, dinner) to generate tailored insights.
chunks.why_it_matters: It simplifies report generation and provides valuable insights into meal consumption patterns, aiding decision-making, optimizing resource allocation, and ensuring accurate and timely management of mess operations.
how_to_use: Navigate to the 'Vision' tab in the Mess Management module.
Filter the report by month and year.
Select either all messes or specific meal types (e.g., breakfast, lunch, dinner).
Download the consolidated report.
examples: Downloading a report for 'January 2023' showing consumption for 'Breakfast' across all messes.
Generating a report for 'Hostel A Mess' for the entire year to analyze trends.

chunks.what_it_does: On the web interface, Mess Console Members or mess administrators can manually enter a meal code provided by a member. The platform then validates the code for the selected meal session, granting or denying meal access accordingly.
chunks.why_it_matters: It provides a manual method for meal redemption via the web interface, ensuring that only valid meal codes are accepted for the correct session, thereby controlling meal distribution.
how_to_use: Manually enter the meal code provided by the member.
The platform checks if the code is valid for the selected meal session.
examples: A mess staff member entering a student's meal code at the counter using a desktop browser.
An administrator validating a guest's meal code through the web portal.

chunks.what_it_does: In the DigiiCampus Mobile Application, Mess Console Members or mess administrators can scan a QR code or manually enter a meal code. The platform automatically verifies the code's validity before granting meal access, providing a quick and efficient redemption process.
chunks.why_it_matters: It offers a convenient and efficient mobile method for meal redemption, including QR code scanning, to quickly verify and grant meal access, improving service speed and user experience.
how_to_use: Scan the QR code or enter the meal code using the DigiiCampus Mobile Application.
The platform automatically verifies the code's validity.
examples: A student presenting their QR code on their phone to a mess staff member who scans it with the DigiiCampus app.
A mess administrator entering a meal code directly into the mobile app for a member.
